assertions.reason: Plan table and every ticket give a single range ('estimate: 120-180 h', 'focused hours (assumption, team new to ADK)'); there is no hands-on vs review-and-verify split and no statement that these are hours for a developer working with a coding agent.

All 20 ticket front-matter estimates equal the plan rows; the goals sum to 1,348-2,104, which equals the phase 1 total, compared with 2,232 h after a 25% reserve: 'Fits at the high end.' The per-role check also adds up.

No calendar-wait field or list. Waits appear only incidentally, such as design Q6 'sandbox tenant is available within three weeks' and G20's prerequisite 'DPIA sign-off', with no durations next to the hours.

G02 (Guidewire discovery) is 'ready' and in M0 in week 3, so Guidewire access starts early. But the DPIA appears only as a G20 GA gate with no early start, and security review is budgeted only as reviewer hours (48-68 of 72) rather than as a calendar wait.

A.arithmetic: Phase 1 goals: G01 40-64, G02 24-40, G03 16-24, G04 40-64, G05 64-100, G06 48-72, G07 48-80, G08 120-180, G09 100-160, G10 120-180, G11 64-100, G12 120-180, G13 80-120, G14 60-100, G15 48-80, G16 100-160, G17 64-100, G18 64-100, G19 48-80, G20 80-120. Sum = 1,348-2,104, matching the stated total. Capacity: 2,400 + 480 + 96 = 2,976; less the 744 h reserve that leaves 2,232, which is correct, and the high end fits with 128 h to spare. Per role: ML engineer 200-300 of 360 and security reviewer 48-68 of 72 both check; engineers get the remainder, 1,100-1,736 of 1,800, which checks. All 20 ticket estimates equal their plan goals. No mismatches found.
A.least_believable_estimate: G01 walking skeleton at 40-64 h (and G05 at 64-100 h for four tools plus a draft table): these are sized like hand-written work by a team new to ADK, with no coding-agent assistance. Overall 1,348-2,104 h is believable without agents but looks inflated for agent-assisted work.

assertions.reason: Every plan goal reads 'human hours, agent-assisted: hands-on X, review and verify Y, total Z'. All 20 tickets carry estimate.hands_on / review_and_verify / total as ranges, and hands-on plus review equals the total in every case checked.

All 20 ticket totals equal the plan rows. The goal sum of 820-1,400 equals the stated phase 1 total and is compared with about 2,120 usable after a 25% reserve: 'It fits at the high end.' The per-person table also sums to 820-1,400.

Every goal and ticket has a separate calendar_waits field, for example G01 'Guidewire sandbox access ... (2-4 weeks); start in week 1', G16 'Guidewire allow-listing of the static egress IP (2-4 weeks)', and 'none' where none apply.

G01 Guidewire access (2-4 weeks) and G03 'DPO/legal review and DPIA sign-off (4-8 weeks); start in week 1' are both started early, and G14 'External pen test booking (3-6 weeks lead)' is scheduled for weeks 11-12. The plan states 'calendar waits are the schedule risk, not hours'.

B.arithmetic: Phase 1 goals: G01 30-50, G02 12-20, G03 16-28, G04 20-32, G05 24-40, G06 24-40, G07 30-50, G08 40-70, G09 60-100, G10 50-90, G11 40-70, G12 120-200, G13 40-70, G14 40-70, G15 24-40, G16 60-100, G17 40-70, G18 40-70, G19 30-50, G20 80-140. Sum = 820-1,400, matching the stated total. Capacity: 2,280 + 456 + 91 = 2,827, rounded to about 2,830; at 75% that is about 2,120, which is correct, and the high end fits with about 720 h unused. Per-person rows check exactly: E1 120-210, E2 114-192, E3 100-173, E4 114-190, E5 160-270, ML 152-260, security 20-35, whole team 40-70, totalling 820-1,400. Usable capacity is 342 each and 68 for the security reviewer, which is correct. One minor gap: the security reviewer's '+ ~10' review hours are outside the phase total. Critical chain G04 -> G06 -> G10 -> G11 -> G19 -> G20 = 254-422, which is correct. hands_on + review_and_verify = total in all 20 tickets. All ticket totals match the plan.
B.least_believable_estimate: G06 versioned draft record, migrations, session DB and tools at 24-40 h, with review time set equal to hands-on time (12-20 / 12-20, the same pattern as G04, G05 and G15) and so looking formulaic. A manager might also question leaving about 35% of usable capacity unplanned, although the plan explains that the slack covers calendar waits.

reasons: B satisfies all four assertions. Every goal and ticket splits hands-on from review-and-verify time, is framed as agent-assisted, and has its own calendar_waits field, with the Guidewire (2-4 wk), DPIA (4-8 wk) and pen-test (3-6 wk) waits started in week 1 or booked ahead. A has single ranges, no hands-on/review split and no calendar-wait treatment.

B is easier to plan people's time from: named owners per goal, a per-person load table that sums exactly to the phase total, a critical-chain figure and a week-by-week calendar sketch. A gives only a per-role check and milestone weeks.

A: No hands-on vs review-and-verify split anywhere; estimates are not stated as coding-agent-assisted hours.
Calendar waits (Guidewire sandbox, DPIA sign-off, Legal copy, GCP project, security sign-off) are never listed with durations. The DPIA appears only as a G20 GA gate, with no early start.
The security reviewer sits at 48-68 of 72 usable hours with no slack, flagged only as 'Barely'.
B: Review time is identical to hands-on time in several goals (G04, G05, G06, G15), which looks formulaic.
The security reviewer's '+ ~10' review hours are left outside the 820-1,400 sum.
About 720 usable hours are left unallocated and engineers are planned at roughly 33-80% of usable capacity. This is justified by the waits, but the plan does not say how idle time is used.
The G08 owner is 'ML engineer with E4' in the ticket but sits only under the ML engineer in the role table.
